title: The cleanroom sits inside a service stack
caption: Air handling, vibration control and utilities occupy separate vertical zones around the process floor. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Air supply above
nodes.detail: Filtered air enters from the ceiling plenum.

nodes.label: Process floor
nodes.detail: Tools operate on a mechanically stable deck.

nodes.label: Subfab services
nodes.detail: Pumps, exhaust and supporting equipment sit below.

nodes.label: Structural foundation
nodes.detail: The building controls vibration and supports heavy equipment.

source.heading: The Building: Why a Fab Is a Vertical Sandwich

title: Move particles away from the wafer environment
caption: Filtered downward airflow dilutes and carries contamination toward return paths; room classification is only one part of wafer protection. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Ceiling filtration
nodes.detail: Filters remove particles from supplied air.

nodes.label: Controlled work zone
nodes.detail: Air moves past tools and protected wafer interfaces.

nodes.label: Return path
nodes.detail: Air leaves through the floor and recirculation system.

title: Protection continues through the wafer handoff
caption: A FOUP and a tool mini-environment protect successive parts of wafer handling inside the cleanroom; they are not layers stacked above the wafer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Closed FOUP
nodes.detail: A carrier protects wafers between processing steps.

nodes.label: Controlled docking
nodes.detail: The carrier connects to the tool through a protected interface.

nodes.label: Tool mini-environment
nodes.detail: Local controls protect the wafer during transfer to the process tool.

title: A lot travels between service points
caption: The AMHS carries FOUPs while dispatch software selects destinations; a stocker buffers lots between operations. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: FOUP at load port
nodes.detail: A carrier holds the wafers as one transport unit.

nodes.label: Overhead vehicle
nodes.detail: The handling system moves it along the rail network.

nodes.label: Stocker or destination
nodes.detail: The lot waits or reaches the next tool.

nodes.label: Tool handoff
nodes.detail: Docking enables controlled wafer transfer.

source.heading: AMHS: How 100,000 Wafers a Month Actually Move

title: A fab route repeatedly revisits tool families
caption: The wafer returns to deposition, patterning and removal with different recipes; the repeating route creates a queueing network. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Deposition visit
nodes.detail: Add the material required by this layer.

nodes.label: Patterning visit
nodes.detail: Define where the next operation acts.

nodes.label: Removal visit
nodes.detail: Transfer or refine the patterned geometry.

nodes.label: Measurement visit
nodes.detail: Check the process result before the next loop.

source.heading: The Process Flow: 1,000–1,500 Steps, Revisited Dozens of Times

title: Utilization is limited by more than purchase price
caption: Installed tools need uptime, a suitable recipe mix and available upstream work to produce qualified wafers. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Installed equipment
nodes.detail: Tool capacity defines the nominal processing resource.

nodes.label: Maintenance and recovery
nodes.detail: Downtime reduces available production time.

nodes.label: Recipe and lot mix
nodes.detail: Work must match the tool's qualified capabilities.

nodes.label: Effective output
nodes.detail: The combination determines usable process capacity.

title: A route becomes executable tool instructions
caption: The manufacturing system tracks the lot while dispatch and equipment control apply the correct recipe and collect history. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Lot identity
nodes.detail: Wafers share a product, route and tracked history.

nodes.label: Manufacturing system
nodes.detail: Software selects and authorizes the next operation.

nodes.label: Tool recipe
nodes.detail: Controlled parameters implement the process step.

nodes.label: Recorded results
nodes.detail: Equipment data and measurements update the lot history.

source.heading: The Lot, the Recipe, and the Software Stack

title: Different teams control different sources of variation
caption: A fab depends on coordinated equipment, process and production work; the roles converge on repeatable output. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Equipment teams
nodes.detail: Maintain tool condition and recover failures.

nodes.label: Process engineers
nodes.detail: Qualify recipes and interpret process variation.

nodes.label: Production teams
nodes.detail: Coordinate lots, priorities and daily execution.

nodes.label: Stable manufacturing
nodes.detail: The combined work sustains qualified production.

title: Every tool depends on a utility network
caption: Power, water, gas and exhaust systems are production inputs, not incidental building services. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Electrical supply
nodes.detail: Tools and environmental systems require continuous power.

nodes.label: Water systems
nodes.detail: Process rinses and cooling serve different water needs.

nodes.label: Gases and exhaust
nodes.detail: Delivery and abatement support controlled chemistry.

nodes.label: Process equipment
nodes.detail: Utility reliability constrains manufacturing availability.

source.heading: Utilities: A Fab Is a Chemical Plant

title: Contamination reaches the wafer through several routes
caption: Gowning reduces human emissions, but tools, chemicals and ambient molecules also need control. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: People and garments
nodes.detail: Movement releases particles and fibers.

nodes.label: Tool surfaces
nodes.detail: Wear and process residues can become contamination.

nodes.label: Chemical environment
nodes.detail: Airborne molecules and input impurities reach surfaces.

nodes.label: Wafer exposure
nodes.detail: Local barriers and clean handling interrupt these paths.

title: A multi-phase fab shares a site backbone
caption: Separate manufacturing phases can share utility infrastructure and connect through transport bridges; this is a conceptual campus layout. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Shared utilities
nodes.detail: Site infrastructure supplies separate manufacturing phases.

nodes.label: Production phase A
nodes.detail: One cleanroom block provides qualified process capacity.

nodes.label: Transport bridge
nodes.detail: Automated material handling moves lots between connected phases.

nodes.label: Production phase B
nodes.detail: Another block can be constructed and ramped separately.

title: A new node advances through evidence gates
caption: Architecture choices become integrated recipes, then yield learning and qualified production; construction alone does not complete a node. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Pathfinding
nodes.detail: Explore device and integration options.

nodes.label: Process development
nodes.detail: Turn the chosen architecture into an integrated flow.

nodes.label: Yield learning
nodes.detail: Find defects and improve process control.

nodes.label: Production ramp
nodes.detail: Expand qualified output after the process is ready.

title: Fixed costs make unused capacity expensive
caption: Equipment costs continue while output changes; maximizing load must still respect queueing delays and process quality. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Fixed installed cost
nodes.detail: Equipment and buildings incur time-based costs.

nodes.label: Qualified wafer output
nodes.detail: Good production spreads those costs over usable product.

nodes.label: Congestion tradeoff
nodes.detail: Very high loading can lengthen waits and cycle time.
